## Framework

The First Officer (FO) recommends a profile, records the user's selection and
variant `kc-dev-flow-2` in the work item, aligns the outcome, and orchestrates.
Spacedock (SD) retains stage state, dispatch, reports, gates, feedback and recovery.
A stage skill defines how its selected profile performs work; it does not
advance state, create authority or substitute for an approval.

| Profile | Intended SD route |
| --- | --- |
| [poc](references/profiles/poc.md) | backlog -> implementation -> validation -> done |
| [pilot](references/profiles/pilot.md) | backlog -> ideation -> implementation -> validation -> done |
| [prod](references/profiles/prod.md) | backlog -> ideation -> implementation -> validation -> done |

Backlog is initial and gated; ideation is gated where present; validation is gated
and fresh, with feedback to implementation; done is terminal. Backlog and done
are state boundaries, not worker stages. SD follows ordered stages, so POC uses
a separate four-stage workflow while Pilot/Prod share the five-stage definition.
Only adopt the needed route. Profile remains a user choice on each task and
selects skill rules, not graph transitions. FO holds a profile/graph mismatch;
that check is an instruction, not a new runtime enforcement mechanism.
POC skips ideation and currently uses independent validation. A POC whose proof
creates state or a seam that must outlive the session records `boundary-crossed:`,
and FO returns that choice to the user at the validation gate. Direct POC
eligibility and special Production recovery are **not implemented or proven**.

## Authority and loading

User authority, approved project AGENTS.md conventions and SD contracts constrain
this framework. Within those boundaries, selected profile principles take
precedence over stage practices, which take precedence over conditional project
learning. If an approved requirement conflicts with the selected profile, return
the affected decision to the user; do not silently change profiles or scope.

Each stage SKILL.md owns its sole declared profile routing table. The FO resolves
the recorded variant/profile before dispatch. A dispatched or reused worker
invokes that variant's exact skill and reads the matching shared profile first,
then stage principles, its stage-specific profile reference, and applicable
adopted project learning. A short final profile reminder is enough; do not load
all profiles or repeat the entire shared rules. Unknown selections, missing
inputs/references or unresolved authority conflicts require a hold report.
These are skill instructions, not mechanically unskippable runtime gates.

Engineering Reviewer provides independent technical assurance; CE (Chief Engineer)
advises the next smallest integrated delivery step. Their agents and skills retain
the existing role boundaries and model table row. Neither is a routine gate,
and POC defaults to no consultation. Observer reads FO's writes to one task's
state against the workflow rules; its agent declares Sonnet, and it reports without
repairing. The design director reviews a ui task's pictures and screenshots and
rules on each decline the author or validator proposes; its agent declares Sonnet, and
it advises and holds no gate. Exact `kc-dev-flow-2:` references prevent
declared links from accidentally selecting the baseline; actual host resolution
still needs a separate behavioral test.

## Design and delivery

FO leads direction and requests research only when it can change a decision;
workers author the bounded deliverable. For a route that includes ideation,
use a PRFAQ with Mermaid whose actors, order, branches and approval boundaries
match the prose. FO's recorded `Surfaces:` line picks the owed artifact: a `ui`
preview, a `db` schema, or `none` for PRFAQ/Mermaid alone;
`scripts/design_surfaces.py check --seed` checks seed fields and the FO record before a new task is
admitted; its default mode checks the markers, the artifacts, a usable
`## Acceptance criteria` section and any `## Captain amendments` before the gate.
A change the Captain makes after accepting a design is recorded there and applied
by the next worker, as [workflow](references/sd/workflow.md) states.
A task that belongs to a release on a journey map triggers one whole-journey review
of that release before its tasks are split; [workflow](references/sd/workflow.md)
gives the signals and the single checkpoint.
Write material corrections back to the same definition before user approval.
Implementation follows approved scope; validation checks the exact result and
returns repairs through the supported feedback route. POC must not gain
an ideation stage or extra design gate through this convention; its boundary
crossing is a report marker, not a design gate.

When work changes retained documents or behavior they describe, stage skills load
one [document reference](references/retained-documents.md) for affected claims,
unique content and rendered diagram agreement. Validation also checks whether
its decisive checks can catch relevant errors, reusing existing counterexamples.
These conditional practices add no mandatory architecture file or global audit.

FO also owns landing a ruling that outlives the task, written by the implementation
worker and checked at validation — see [workflow](references/sd/workflow.md)'s
Decision records. A capability a user will get, named in conversation and
deferred, belongs on the product's journey map instead.

The [workflow source](references/sd/workflow.md) defines limited FO design
corrections and nonblocking dispositions. Template adoption grants no editing
permission; approved decisions and worker evidence remain protected.

Continuous stage-pin sealing and its kernel loader are intentionally omitted.
Git history and SD records do not prove which content was used at a historical
stage entry. This package does not fix the baseline's skipped-pin bug or
claim equivalent tamper detection.

Optional tools join as extensions in [`extensions/`](extensions/), each described by its

workflow's `## Extensions` section is the rule FO follows. The template lists the `required`
rows; the install ask in [`adoption.md`](references/sd/adoption.md) offers the rest, and
`scripts/lint-skills.py` checks that the `required` rows and the template line agree.

| Extension | Tier | Joins | Adds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [codex](extensions/codex/EXTENSION.md) | recommended | FO review rounds and the merge ask | reads Codex GitHub review rounds on the PR head |
| [roborev](extensions/roborev/EXTENSION.md) | recommended | implementation, before the report | a local roborev review of the committed changes |
| [peers](extensions/peers/EXTENSION.md) | required | FO, before opening a task or exchanging peer facts | selects the peer transport, permits confirmed Paseo asks and replies without paseo listing, searches existing work and checks facts within existing authority |

| [journey-map](extensions/journey-map/EXTENSION.md) | recommended | FO, after a gate ruling on a journey task, before `merge guard`, and after the archive | writes a footprint for a ruling that answers a map question, checks it before the merge guard, and folds it into the map as a docs-only pull request |
| [release-acceptance](extensions/release-acceptance/EXTENSION.md) | recommended, with journey-map | the idle look prompts unclaimed walks; an acceptance task runs from implementation to the validation gate and the close | walks a finished release with reviewers on different Claude models, has the design director rule on their complaints and the deferred findings, and records the walk in the task folder |
| [fo-feedback](extensions/fo-feedback/EXTENSION.md) | optional, requires peers | interviewing maintainer, at attended resume and named batch close | gathers operator experience every three completed batches beside independent observer findings |

## Learning loop

Optional [operator feedback](extensions/fo-feedback/EXTENSION.md) records failures,
workarounds and useful events; findings follow the existing backlog and Captain decisions.

The loop runs on three lines. Project learning: `learn` evaluates one closed task and
may propose a root learning.md rule as a Draft PR. Package improvement: the
[observer](skills/observer/SKILL.md) reads what FO wrote into one task's state
against the workflow rules, at archive and when a maintainer reads an adopter's first
task after a release, and a rule broken in two tasks becomes a package change under
`maintain-flow`. Deciding for the Captain: `scripts/decision_ledger.py` derives every
gate ruling from the task files SD already writes, and FO decides only within the
delegation ladder of [ADR 0011](https://github.com/iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins/blob/main/docs/adr/0011-fo-decides-for-the-captain-by-a-delegation-ladder.md);
[ADR 0009](https://github.com/iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins/blob/main/docs/adr/0009-self-improvement-is-a-three-position-switch-unlocked-by-change-class.md)
keeps package self-improvement manual.

Use [`kc-dev-flow-2:learn`](skills/learn/SKILL.md) for one explicitly named closed
task. FO verifies committed SD archive state and the original repository-qualified
merged GitHub PR through existing read interfaces, then delegates independent
evaluation. Missing or contradictory evidence holds learning without reopening
the development task. This is skill-led verification; the Python helper still
records supplied facts and does not authenticate SD or GitHub.

Use [`kc-dev-flow-2:evaluate-learning`](skills/evaluate-learning/SKILL.md) for a
bounded independent assessment of explicitly supplied task evidence. Its three
outcomes are add, no-change and remove; a rewrite combines remove/add. Entries
contain Applicability, Practice and Evidence. One task supports one case; reading
a rule or green tests alone does not prove improvement. No applicable case is
not grounds for deletion, and unknown attribution stays unknown. Fixed project
rules require separate user-approved adoption into AGENTS.md; no auto-promotion,
scores or maturity system is introduced.

The skill documents the strict evidence-pack and evaluation JSON formats and
commands for `scripts/learning.py`. This stdlib helper records eligibility from
caller-supplied closure/merge facts; it does **not** verify SD or GitHub truth.
It stores one atomic record under the Git common directory's
`kc-dev-flow-2/learning/`, shared by linked worktrees in the same clone. An opaque
claim token binds completion to its pending attempt. Invalid results leave that
claim repairable; duplicate triggers observe it rather than launch another job.
A store-wide lock also serializes new claims against each other: while one job's
directory has a torn or missing record, its evaluation is pending, or its
completed proposal has no settled delivery (merged, closed, or explicitly
released), a `claim` for any other job in the same store is refused, naming the
blocking job. Re-claiming the same job is unaffected. A proposal the Captain
declines to deliver needs an explicit `release`; no CLI command removes or
rewrites `release.json`, so a release cannot be undone. A closed delivery
cannot be released; a released job whose delivery was missing or confirmed
absent can still later be observed `open` (a PR turns up that the release
believed did not exist) — that observation blocks again, because a release
stops a job from blocking, it does not stop the provider from reporting new
facts about it.
A completed record contains both evaluation and local proposal; no-change has no
proposal. No recorder command writes learning.md, AGENTS.md or workflow state.

Pending ownership is not process liveness. Torn/missing records are uncertain;
recovery requires a current record digest and an explicit caller attestation
that the prior owner stopped. It preserves prior bytes and revokes the old token.
Completed results cannot be replaced through this CLI. POSIX file locking and
atomic replacement cover cooperating callers on local filesystems, not separate
clones, distributed locks or protection from a process with the same file access.

A changed result can be materialized by an author in an owned isolated worktree,
changing only root learning.md. The evaluated integration commit/learning blob
must still match before publication. User commit and delivery authority remain
required; a no-change result creates no branch or PR. A job-derived branch/body
marker supports all-state PR lookup. Reuse a fully matching existing PR; conflicting
or unknown provider evidence holds rather than sending another one.

The recorder keeps delivery ownership/observations in a separate atomic sidecar,
leaving completed evaluation bytes immutable. It binds the reviewed result, repo,
branch, candidate and learning blobs, plus exact PR title/body. Claiming records
uncertainty before remote effects; existing claims grant no automatic resend.
FO uses existing Git/gh commands to publish a Draft PR and record observed state.
A failed response does not prove the send failed. Explicit stopped-owner recovery
requires a current digest and successful provider reconciliation; unknown stays
held, matched PRs are reused and merged observations cannot regress through the
CLI. These are local consistency checks over caller-attested provider facts.

On `dev` or `learn` invocation, `learning.py notices` exposes unread results,
including no-change, pending and uncertain states. FO acknowledges a snapshot
only after presenting it; a changed digest remains unread. `notices --all` also
makes acknowledged jobs available for explicit inspection/recovery. Read-only
queries create no learning directory when none exists. Context injection alone
is not notification, and a crash before acknowledgement can repeat a notice.

A receipt or PR is not an active practice. Subsequent work reads the currently
adopted integration version of learning.md, after its separately authorized
review/merge path. A recorded merge does not prove a practice improves future
work. Harness hooks, automatic polling/background launch, issue reporting and
cross-clone deduplication remain future work; the notice step is not an every-host
SessionStart guarantee. See the learn skill for the fixed CLI plan/observation
schemas, provider checks, recovery and exact delivery authority boundaries.

## Maintenance and evidence

These are source-repository maintenance commands, not standalone installed-plugin
commands. They depend on the repository-level `scripts/skill-frontmatter-lint.sh`
and its dependencies. Run from a complete checkout's repository root:

```sh
python3 kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/lint-skills.py
python3 kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/test_sd_dispatch.py --sd-plugin-root /absolute/path/to/active-spacedock
```

Every other test file is listed in `.github/workflows/kc-dev-flow-2-tests.yml`, which
CI runs on each change to this package; run the same commands from there.
[`kc-dev-flow-2:maintain-flow`](skills/maintain-flow/SKILL.md) holds the rules for
changing the package: the workflow word budget, behaviour replay and observing adopters.

Lint reuses `scripts/skill-frontmatter-lint.sh` scoped to this tree and checks
declared route coverage, applicability values, exact paths, required principles
and skill namespaces, and that every package script named in `skills/` and
`references/` is written `<package>/scripts/NAME` and that a skill using `<package>`
carries a `Package root:` line. It does not parse rule prose or prove route-following,
unknown-profile refusal, gate execution or cross-host parity.
The [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) defines
frontmatter and directory conventions; complete format validation is a separate
authoring check, not a claim made by this CLI.

The [adoption reference](references/sd/adoption.md) uses SD commission/refit,
split-root state, code worktrees and the activated SD package's unmodified
`pr-merge` mod. The mod is installed into the adopting workflow, not vendored here.
The workflow's delivery rules preserve project Draft PR, CI and manual merge
requirements and restrict unapproved fallback; those are FO instructions, not new
mechanical controls. Adoption checks actual `merge: pr-merge` hook discovery before
activation: SD can finalize locally when no hook or blocking record exists.

The CLI test copies the workflow source into disposable code/state repositories.
It checks six stage/host handoffs, stage-definition fetches, PRFAQ/Mermaid gate
context, the `## Dispatch facts` section, finding disposition and delivery authority,
that scope notes naming the package root reach the dispatch file ahead of the checklist,
and that a report ending `- FAILED: none.` is refused by SD and named by its
checklist read, and that a correction without a Summary is refused until a complete report follows. Both route graphs across three profiles exercise synthetic gate
successors and stamped implementation / validation worktree reuse. Fresh validation is declared configuration, not an
executed independent worker. Copied canonical hook discovery and merge-guard
arming pass; the missing-hook control demonstrates local finalization's limit.
Existing wrong-stage, removed-stage, AC-scanner and host-marker controls remain.
`--keep` retains successful repos and raw evidence; failure evidence is retained
by default. Synthetic approvals and local archive controls are test inputs,
not real user acceptance, hook execution or remote delivery. No prompt is sent
to a model. A real project still needs approved configuration and observed merge.

For an authorized native Claude trial, remove foreign markers for that process
only: `env -u CODEX_THREAD_ID -u PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR claude <approved arguments>`.
Use the exact isolated repository as cwd, name its workflow explicitly in the FO
assignment, and retain `--workflow-dir` on SD commands. Do not change the parent
environment or add a wrapper. The model-free marker check is not a rerun of the
native trial, and a failed stamped dispatch must not be assumed mutation-free.
Before a future live run, verify the selected SD plugin and executable versions;
an updated skill cache alone does not establish a comparable runtime.
At ideation, retain user gate approval while proposing routine implementation
details within accepted scope; escalate material changes rather than every detail.

Future comparisons must include host behavior, retained route exceptions and
learning/review costs as well as removed files. This slice runs no model

or removal? Check that remaining surfaces map to the goal, a named falsifier,
safety boundary or required lifecycle obligation; a deletion earns its place by
the same standard as retention. Use existing evidence, not a new proof harness.

the code beside it, cites a line number or marks a section is a repair finding.

and report its output. Exit 1 (a ratio above the maximum, or a comment citing task
numbering, review provenance, a PR or issue number or a `file:line`) is a repair
finding returned through feedback; exit 2 is a configuration error that returns to FO.

implementation cycles you validate, and run

record (its exit 1), or a requirement in it that traces to no accepted criterion or

changed screen at the candidate; reading the code or a passing render test is not

A dispatch built with `dispatch build --stamp` leaves <task>/dispatch/<stage>-<cycle>.md written from the same checklist, scope notes, model and SHA it sends, so the record no longer depends on FO remembering it.

## Scope

- Source: the Captain 「開」 (chat, 2026-11-06), answering 「要開這 4 張嗎？」 after fo-feedback round 005 (.notes/fo-feedback/round-005.md, closed 2026-11-06).
- Bite: kc-paseo-plugins reconstructed every dispatch record of batch r1b-polish-1 after the fact (_archive/project-env-rate-limit-cause/dispatch/ideation-1.md: "Reconstructed by FO on 2026-11-06, after the dispatch"; FO read 2026-11-06); qnow sent a follow-up addendum with no record (observer); the kc-plugin FO wrote one message record late and omitted required lines in batches 14 and 15 (observer reports).
- Upstream first: Spacedock dispatch build --stamp (Spacedock is not the Captain's repository: a change there is an upstream issue, so the dev2 side may be a package wrapper); kc-dev-flow-2 dispatch_records.py, which checks the record.
- Non-goals: follow-up messages to a running worker (a separate record kind).

## Budget
- One package PR; the workflow word budget does not rise unless the design names a raise for the Captain.

## Stop condition
- A stamped dispatch leaves a record that dispatch_records.py accepts without FO writing it, or the design names why Spacedock cannot and what the package does instead.

## FO alignment

Alignment: needed at ideation; the design choice is his to accept.
Result: aligned at backlog: Batch 17 backlog sitting, the Captain 「核准（建議）」 (host question dialog, 2026-11-07), answering 「決定：第 17 批這五張（Paseo 瀏覽器當工人驗收的預設、決策紀錄檢查分清驗證取代與指向依據、派工時自動寫派工紀錄、沒給範圍時設計檢查說沒跑、觀察者列出沒有合併提問紀錄的合併）都用 Pilot，照各自寫下的範圍、預算與停止條件進入構想嗎？建議核准。要改哪張直接說。」, approved the outcome and bounds in this file; the design choice the Alignment line names stays his at the ideation gate.
Surfaces: none
Visible change: none
Release review: not needed: workflow maintenance, on no journey map.

### Existing-code check

Completeness: `dispatch build --stamp` works through the journey and writes no record; `dispatch_records.py` works as a checker; no record writer exists (two bounded searches: the Spacedock `## Hook:` and `dispatch/<stage>` greps, and the package and adopter `dispatch build` greps above; excluded: `_archive/` evidence copies). Need: the Scope bite, three sessions with records written late, reconstructed or short of required lines. The design adds one script and reuses `dispatch_records.py`'s checks unchanged, and `task_folder` from `design_surfaces.py`.

### What changes

One package PR:

- `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/dispatch_stage.py` (new). Arguments: `--workflow-dir`, `--entity-path`, `--stage`, `--checklist-file`, `--scope-notes-file`, optional `--feedback-context-file`/`--feedback-reflow`/`--advance` passed through, `--model TEXT` (required), `--roster TEXT`, `--candidate SHA` (repeatable, 40 hex or exit 2), `--symptom TEXT`, `--spacedock BIN` (default `$SPACEDOCK_BIN`, then `spacedock`).
  - Writes `# <stage>-<N>`, `Dispatched: <git -C workflow-dir rev-parse HEAD> (workflow checkout)`, `Model:`, then the given `Roster:`, `Candidate:` and `Symptom:` lines, `## Checklist` with the checklist file, `## Scope notes` with the scope-notes file. It never edits either file's text: an omitted `Package root:` or completion line is held by the checker, before any build.
  - N: let M be the highest `<stage>-<M>.md` committed at the state checkout's HEAD (message records excluded). N = M, writing nothing, only when that file's bytes equal what would be written and the state checkout's HEAD commit is the one that added it (an immediate retry after a sync or assembly failure); otherwise N = M + 1, 1 when none, overwriting an uncommitted file at N. Any state commit in between makes an identical dispatch a new record, so `role_triggers.py` still counts a repeated round.
  - `--note TEXT` appends `, TEXT` inside the `Dispatched:` parentheses, for the README version and batch annotations FO writes today.
  - Runs `dispatch_records.py <task folder>` and `--names --strict <record>` as subprocesses with the same Python; on success it prints nothing of theirs.
  - Without `--advance`, runs `<spacedock> dispatch build --stamp` with the build flags; with it, `dispatch build --advance` and then `<spacedock> state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`. Stdout is the build's envelope.
- `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/test_dispatch_stage.py` (new): split-root git fixtures with the README from `references/sd/workflow.md`, run against `$SPACEDOCK_BIN`; exits nonzero naming `SPACEDOCK_BIN` when it is unset, so CI cannot pass it by skipping.
- `.github/workflows/kc-dev-flow-2-tests.yml`: one step after "Install pinned Spacedock", `SPACEDOCK_BIN="$HOME/.local/bin/spacedock" python3 kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/test_dispatch_stage.py`. Cost per PR: not measured.
- `kc-dev-flow-2/references/sd/workflow.md` (Stages): three passages replaced, text below.
- `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/lint-skills.py`: one `WORKFLOW_BUDGET_STEPS` entry, `delta=-2`, why "dispatch_stage.py saves and checks the record; the README names the script and its flags".
- `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/test_sd_dispatch.py`: the `dispatch-record` and `resumed-dispatch` entries' `need` and `swaps` follow the new text. `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/test_dispatch_records.py`: `ContextNoticeTests.PARAGRAPH` follows the new third passage.
- ADR, only if the Captain accepts D1 (the number reserved at implementation dispatch), short title `stage-worker-dispatches-are-built-by-a-package-script-that-writes-their-record`. Draft: **Decision:** FO builds each stage-worker dispatch with `dispatch_stage.py`, which writes the record from the build's own inputs, checks it, and lets the stamp commit carry it; Spacedock is unchanged. **Context:** the Scope bite; the Chain check. **Consequences:** like ADR 0014, prose-enforced: an FO that follows Spacedock's skill text instead writes no record, and `dispatch_records.py --coverage` still holds that task after the report. Reopen on ADR 0014's condition, a dispatch-time hook in Spacedock. **Protects:** `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/dispatch_stage.py` — `main`. **Words:** the Captain's ruling on D1.

New README text, replacing "FO saves those scope notes … fixes each part it lists.", "A follow-up message … never a pointer to another record." and "Before `dispatch build`, FO runs … on stderr.":

> FO builds each worker dispatch with `python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_stage.py`: `dispatch build`'s flags, `--model`, and `--roster`, `--candidate` or `--symptom` where owed. It saves the checklist, scope notes, model and the SHA it dispatches from as `<task>/dispatch/<stage>-<cycle>.md`, so the instruction a worker followed outlives the session that wrote it, checks it as below, then builds; the build's commit carries the record.
>
> A follow-up message to a worker FO resumes is a dispatch too, saved by hand as `<stage>-<cycle>-message-<n>.md` with a checklist of the items it asks, never a pointer to another record, and committed with `spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`.
>
> Each record passes `python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py <task folder>` and `--names --strict <record>` before a worker reads it; nonzero holds dispatch. Relative script paths are allowed; bare package script names remain errors. Plain `--names` preserves existing historical verdicts and reports skipped context checks on stderr.

Not changed: `dispatch_records.py`, `extensions/paseo/EXTENSION.md` (its "chain … onto that same build command" now chains onto the script, which is that build command), `_mods/`, Spacedock.

### Words FO reads at each moment

Counted as `len(text.split())` over whitespace-normalized text, the count `lint-skills.py` uses; base origin/main 139feeaee (`lint-skills.py` exit 0, "5933 of 5933 words").

| startup and resume (README read whole) | 5933 | 5931 |
| fresh worker dispatch: README passages | 112 (passages 1 and 3) | 101 (passages 1 and 3) |
| fresh worker dispatch: script output on a complete record | 4 ("N dispatch record(s) complete") | 0 |
| follow-up message: README passages | 143 (all three; passage 2's "the same check" needs passage 1) | 83 (passages 2 and 3) |

Spacedock's own dispatch text (`claude-fo-dispatch.md`) is read in both and unchanged. The script's docstring is read only through `--help`.

### Non-goals and limits

- Follow-up messages (Scope non-goal); deriving `Model:` from the roster (D2); moving `package_version.py` and `workflow_checkout.py` into the script (D3); an upstream Spacedock issue; filling omitted scope-note lines.
- An FO that runs `spacedock dispatch build` directly, as Spacedock's skill text says, writes no record; `--coverage` catches it after the report, as today. This PR does not show FO uses the script: the first batch after release shows it (each fresh record's adding commit subject is `dispatch: <slug> entering <stage>`).
- An identical rerun with no state commit since the record was added reuses its number; a re-dispatch after any later state commit, such as a worker report, is a new record.
- The `Model:` and `Roster:` text stays FO-typed; a wrong value is not caught, as today.
- No new profile obligation: no production data, credentials or unattended operation.

### Needs decision

- **D1: build dispatches through a package script (this design), not an upstream Spacedock change, and land the ADR above.** Recommend yes. It is the only route the package owns, and it works on the pinned 0.27.2 today. Worse under it: Spacedock's skill still tells FO to call `dispatch build`, so the README must win that conflict; FO runs one more script per dispatch; a later Spacedock change to `entityCommitPaths` would break the commit seam, caught by AC-1 in CI.

# Chief engineer advice: preserve the complete dispatch commit scope

Recommendation: **adjust**. Add one fail-closed check for the complete task commit scope before the wrapper writes anything, then exercise that boundary through the real builder. Checking only the reused record's index would leave the same loss mechanism reachable through other task files.

```yaml
chief_engineer_advice:
  outcome: A Pilot stage dispatch records its actual inputs in the stamp commit without consuming or destroying pre-existing task work.
  next_step: Add a shared clean-task-scope precondition before select_record, covering fresh dispatch, retry and advance; prove preservation with the real pinned builder and scoped state comparisons.
  material_risk: Another writer can change a scoped file or index entry after a one-time check; the proposed check is not a transaction lock.
  decision_needed: FO owns routing the repair and ensuring exclusive same-task writes during dispatch; no new Captain decision is needed within that boundary.
  defer:
    - Upstream Spacedock changes or a general multi-writer transaction system, unless exclusive same-task writes cannot be established.
    - Model and roster derivation, separate version preflights, and automatic follow-up records, as already excluded.
  recommendation: adjust
```

## Evidence and route

Read at product head `0d84d5d1b96fd674dba3a442d69c2e7898cceccd`, branch `spacedock-ensign/dispatch-build-writes-the-dispatch-record`, in `/Users/kent/conductor/workspaces/kc-claude-plugins/colombo/.context/dev2-adoption/worktree/.worktrees/spacedock-ensign-dispatch-build-writes-the-dispatch-record`; its working tree was clean. Assigned base: `334d91e3165953b2ca7191e3308d80b6c02c4a99`. Workflow checkout remains `ba055b8a7a55a787ac989c4cef52d07dd75661ad`. Task state is `validation`, profile `pilot` (bounded real use).

The accepted task design and architecture decision record (ADR) 0070 retain the package wrapper and Spacedock's existing commit seam. ADR 0027 places structured checks at the write; ADRs 0014, 0037 and 0048 retain separate preflights, work ownership and First Officer (FO) publication authority. This advice changes repair sequencing within those boundaries; it grants no gate, validation, merge or release approval.

At `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/dispatch_stage.py:46–54`, identical retry returns before the new-path index check; exclusive creation protects only a new record. At lines 58–65, cleanup removes an invocation-created record and its index entry if absent from HEAD. Neither protects other paths the builder stages. The supplied `validation-2/retry-index-probe.json` shows success with a changed index blob, unchanged working bytes and unchanged HEAD; the refusal control preserves all three. I inspected these artifacts, not reran the probe.

The validator's retained Spacedock 0.27.2 source, `/tmp/pr812-validation2.gfsHcD/spacedock-4d158a484ec73e184861067f8ed1e20087fdc26a`, confirms the broader boundary: `internal/dispatch/stamp.go:247–264` runs path-scoped `git add -A` before commit; `entityCommitPaths` at lines 322–335 includes the flat task file plus its companion directory, or the entire folder-form task directory. Inline stamping uses the same pattern at lines 217–235. Advance's later state commit also stages its entity unit (`internal/cli/state_sync.go:359–433`). Thus a staged-only edit to the task file, an older dispatch or a review/report file can encounter the same mechanism. That broader reach is a source inference, not a newly executed reproduction.

## One precondition before any write

Require **the entire resolved commit scope to be clean against HEAD in both the index and worktree**, with no pre-existing untracked content that the stamp would add. Define the scope from the builder's entity unit, including the companion directory that record creation will introduce; do not reduce it to the chosen record or `dispatch/`.

- For every tracked path in that scope, HEAD, the index and the worktree must agree in content, existence and Git-relevant type/mode. Refuse staged changes, unstaged changes, staged-only changes with worktree restored to HEAD, partial staging, additions, deletions, renames and unresolved index entries. Even equal staged/worktree edits differing from HEAD are refused: they are pre-existing work, not owned by this dispatch.
- For paths absent from HEAD, refuse existing index entries or nonignored untracked files in the scope. Independently require the selected new record path to be absent, retaining exclusive creation; ignored files or dangling symlinks must not let that path be overwritten. Reuse is allowed only after the scope passes, and still requires the current adding-commit and expected-input rules.
- Resolve the actual state repository and canonical task layout; use literal, NUL-safe path handling. Inspect both comparisons (index versus HEAD and worktree versus index), plus untracked paths. A command failure or unresolved scope is a hold, not an empty result. Do not rely solely on a status shortcut that can hide `assume-unchanged` or `skip-worktree` entries: verify their content explicitly or refuse those scoped entries. Refuse an unsupported path escape/type instead of declaring it clean.

Call this once after read-only argument/scope resolution and **before `select_record`**, including its directory creation, so fresh, reused, changed-input and `--advance` paths all pass it. On refusal, name the path and staged/unstaged condition, return nonzero with `dispatch_stage: dispatch not built;`, emit no envelope and invoke neither builder nor cleanup. Preserve the existing ownership restriction on cleanup; do not add automatic reset, stash or commit as a remedy.

Why this closes the pre-existing-state class: every admitted pre-existing scoped version is already represented by HEAD, and there is no additional staged or worktree version for staging to replace. The wrapper then creates only its own record before the builder's authorized task mutation. This is deliberately more conservative than allowing any state where index happens to equal worktree.

**Concurrency limit:** no check performed only once can guarantee preservation against a writer acting after it. Exclusive same-task ownership must last through build/commit/cleanup. Git's transient `index.lock` retry in `stamp.go:353–371` does not provide that ownership across the sequence. If FO cannot establish it, hold and return that concrete constraint for an isolated state checkout or coordinated upstream transaction design; another record-specific condition cannot solve it.

## Cost to normal use

A clean task and clean immediate retry keep the same invocation and numbering. Local Git reads add unmeasured latency and no network request. Pending edits anywhere in this task now hold dispatch, even when they could safely have been committed together; FO must have their owner preserve/reconcile and intentionally commit them first. In particular, blindly running `state commit` on divergent staged/worktree content would repeat the loss and is not a safe recovery instruction. Do not require unrelated tasks or the whole code checkout to be clean. Explain the remedy in the refusal diagnostic; no new workflow gate or word-budget increase is needed.

## Proof required for the next repair

Extend the existing real-binary suite with a table-driven preservation matrix; retain the accepted success and failure tests.

1. **Locations and routes:** apply dirty-state cases to the new record path, reused committed record, older dispatch, task frontmatter and nested companion report. Exercise flat and folder-form tasks, fresh dispatch, immediate retry, new round and advance. A clean selected record with a dirty sibling must hold.
2. **States:** cover index-only change, worktree-only change, index/worktree equal but different from HEAD, index/worktree each different, and the reported worktree-equals-HEAD case. Include untracked files, staged additions with/without a worktree file, staged/unstaged deletions, renames across the scope boundary, conflicts and type/mode changes. Cover the special flags and literal-path cases used by the implementation. This derives cases from the three representations, rather than adding only another retry fixture.
3. **Refusal oracle:** snapshot HEAD, all scoped file bytes/existence/modes, semantic index entries (blob, mode, stage and relevant flags), and outside-scope sentinel state. Assert nonzero, named diagnostic, empty stdout, no builder call, no new record or frontmatter change, and preservation of every snapshot. Run dirty cases with otherwise valid inputs so refusal cannot be credited to the record checker.
4. **Allowed and recovery paths:** real 0.27.2 builder commits matching inputs from a clean scope; immediate retry reuses; changed inputs or a later commit mint the next number; advance commits before its envelope. Unrelated staged and unstaged task work stays intact and outside the dispatch commit. An owner-reconciled/committed task becomes dispatchable. Checker failure, staged-then-failed build, and committed-then-assembly failure retain the existing cleanup/retry contracts.
5. **Falsifiers and integration:** remove the guard; omit the index comparison; omit worktree/untracked inspection; narrow scope to the selected record or dispatch directory; place the guard after record creation; bypass it on retry or advance. Each mutant must fail the matching preservation assertion. Run the unchanged acceptance chain plus these cases on the new exact head, then obtain the existing hosted real-binary check. Use a controlled overlapping-writer probe to establish any concurrency claim; otherwise retain the exclusive-writer limitation explicitly.

# 0026. Role calls are owed on counts read from task records, and a dated call clears them whatever it says

Date: 2026-10-20

## Status

Accepted

## Context

`role_triggers.py` owed a chief-engineer call on a `- Cycle N` line under `### Feedback Cycles` and cleared a call only when its question named `Cycle 3` or `Amendment N`. Over 38 window tasks in four repositories it read 0 events in the two that record cycles in stage-report headings, and it refused 3 of the 4 calls FO had made (two worded "third repair cycle", one filed under another heading). The Captain's direction on 2026-10-20 was counts from structured records, not keywords. The measurement, the per-task table and the falsified alternatives are in the task's `## Design`. This supersedes the wording-match clause of the special-role-triggers design (PR #664), which has no ADR of its own to amend.

## Decision

**Words:** 「設計時不應該過度依賴關鍵字，而是可能要依靠犯錯字數觸發，合理嗎？」 — Captain, 2026-10-20, chat; 「先加第一個，第二個列入評估」 — Captain, 2026-10-20, chat, on the engineering-reviewer model rule and the security-reviewer evaluation; at the ideation gate, 2026-10-20, D1 「同意」, D2 「第四輪」, D3 「Ａ」, D4 「Ａ」, D5 「同意」, each as the gate question recommended.

**Options considered:**
- Chief-engineer is owed at four repair passes, read as `## Stage Report: implementation` headings minus one (chosen, D2); three passes fires one more false case (go-live-consent); a sent-back count added one case and needs a free-text verdict match that leaves 105 of 410 validation reports unreadable; same-path review rounds, holds or overrides, ADR-draft headings and cross-references added no unique true catch or false-fired
- Engineering-reviewer keeps its replacing-amendment event, one line per task, cleared by a call dated no earlier than the amendment on a model no lower than the one required, or by a dated waiver (chosen)
- Model: Fable when the frontmatter says `profile: prod` or the `Surfaces:` line lists `db`, else Opus, never lower (chosen, D4); path or secret signals were not chosen (the authority-path signal marks 31 of 38 tasks, secrets have no field)
- Review rounds, two review ids with inline findings on an open task PR, also owe chief-engineer, as a last separate slice (chosen, D1)
- The four engineering-reviewer cases no count sees stay with judgment and no `Reverses:` line is added (chosen, D3)
- ADR 0021 D1 stays: stage 1 of the evaluation reads saved reports and runs no model, stage 2 waits for its result (chosen, D5)

**Recommended:** each of D1 to D5 as the gate question stated, which the Captain accepted.

A call or a waiver counts only as a `Reviewer:` line under `## FO alignment`, and a call counts by its date and model, not by its question. Later work that changes what owes a role call reads counts from committed task records and does not match phrases.

## Consequences

FO is told once per task and role, in the line `pr_watch.py tasks` already prints, until the call is recorded. A call on another question dated after an amendment now clears it. A count cannot see an authority change, a ruling reversed in another task or a new authority surface; those stay with the Captain and FO. The thresholds are in-sample on one 38-task window judged by four observers. Reopen when a batch shows an owed case the count missed twice in the same shape, or a false fire on a task whose extra passes were phases.

Amended 2026-10-22 (Captain: 「可以」 at the ideation gate of the task `merge-ask-holds-missing-clauses`, narrowing it to this one hold; 「按建議**不算**」 on D2): `delivery_gate.py check` runs `role_triggers.py` on the task folder and stem, without `--review-rounds`, and holds the merge ask while the committed task owes a chief-engineer call (four repair passes) or an engineering-reviewer call (a replacing amendment): exit 1 adds one problem line and the script's `next:` lines, exit 2 holds with its message (「可以」). Review rounds do not hold the ask; idle still prints that call (「按建議不算」). The script reads the task as committed, so an amendment not yet state-committed is not seen and a call not yet state-committed does not clear. "Told once per task and role" above still describes the idle line; a skipped call now also refuses the merge ask until the call or a dated waiver is committed.

Amended 2026-10-25 (Captain: 「都開」 on 2026-10-23 and 「可以」 on 2026-10-25 for the task `role-triggers-owe-ce-on-review-drift`; 「全准」 at its ideation gate on 2026-10-25, accepting D1 and D2 as the gate question recommended): a review-round event is cleared only by a chief-engineer call or waiver dated no earlier than the UTC date of the newest review round, which `pr_watch.py tasks` reads from the one comment list it already fetches and passes as `--drift-date`; a call about something else made before that round no longer clears it, and no file-path test is used (D1). A call made earlier on the same date as that round still clears it. Without `--drift-date` any call or waiver clears, as before; the repair-pass event keeps its undated clear. The merge ask still does not count review rounds (D2).

Amended 2026-11-02: Astra meets the Fable floor, and chief-engineer calls need opus rank or above, for both repair-pass and review-round events. The date and waiver rules stay as recorded above; see ADR 0049 for the Captain's words and the accepted model table.

Amended 2026-11-02 (Captain: 「可以」, answering 「決定：多開「完成通知」和「挑剔使用者可用 Gemini」兩張票，先前五件事照建議，可以嗎？」 at the ideation revision of `second-round-prompts-a-step-back`; then 「照建議」, answering 「決定：五張設計進實作、Gemini 這張停在這裡，四個決定都照建議嗎？要改哪件直接說。」 at its ideation approval): two validation reports with a Material or Needs decision F bullet, or two amendments whose `Supersedes:` does not start with `none`, print the three questions at idle and merge without a hold. The counts stay separate. D1 follows this record's structured-count rule and ADR 0045's F-bullet form, accepting that 5 of 13 word-detected tasks stay silent; replacing amendments count, not every relaxation. At either count's third occurrence, D2 follows the repair/amendment merge hold and existing waiver, rather than review rounds' non-hold; D3 assigns chief-engineer because an engineering-reviewer call already clears amendments whatever its question. Its one owed line carries: is what I am solving still the outcome first asked for; can this gap be tested now, or am I waiting; what breaks if this criterion or process is deleted? The opus-rank floor applies, Astra included. A call or waiver dated no earlier than the third amendment clears that event, reusing the drift-date rule; any qualifying call or waiver clears failed validations, reusing the undated repair rule. A fourth occurrence owes no second call; engineering-reviewer's amendment event stays separate. At count two, questions repeat on each run without an answer record; at three or more, a cleared event prints no reminder.

Amended 2026-11-02 (Captain: 「照建議」, answering 「決定：四件事都照建議嗎？要改哪件直接說。」 after FO proposed 「修這兩個 bug，在原本的票裡修」, recorded in `second-round-prompts-a-step-back` Captain amendment 1): each count reaches its own reminder threshold independently. A cleared event at three or more does not suppress the other event's second-occurrence reminder. Suppress a duplicate reminder only when an emitted owed-call line already carries the three questions; all model, date, waiver and merge-hold rules above remain.

Amended 2026-11-03 (Captain: 「可以」, answering 「決定：七張設計照建議進實作，但驗收到期提醒的 D7 改成『在 kc-journey-map 登記 journey-progress/v1，預算放寬為兩個 PR，kc-journey-map 那個先合併』，可以嗎？」 at the ideation gate of `diagnosis-rounds-count-toward-step-back`, accepting its D1 and D2 as recommended): dispatch records count diagnosis rounds by stage and normalized `Symptom:` header, trimming and collapsing spaces and casefolding; values starting with `none`, fenced lines and body lines do not count. At round two, `dispatch_records.py` prints the three step-back questions on stderr before each dispatch, following ADR 0027's placement at the write; folder mode checks each stage's highest-numbered record, and `--names` counts only through the named record. A record numbered two or higher without the header gets a stderr hint; only `--names --strict` holds it (D1). Idle and merge read committed records: round two advises without a hold, round three owes chief-engineer and holds the merge ask (D2). An opus-rank-or-above call or waiver under `## FO alignment`, dated no earlier than the third record's first `Dispatched:` date, clears that symptom's later rounds too; without that date any qualifying call or waiver clears. Other event families remain independent; an owed line carrying the questions suppresses duplicate reminders. With the replay's symptom name, measured added words are 48 per dispatch reminder, 21 per missing-header hint, 47 at idle/merge round two and 74 at round three; a clean dispatch, startup, after archive and the workflow template add zero. The workflow word budget is unchanged. Renamed symptoms and multiple browser runs inside one dispatch remain outside the count.

Clarified 2026-11-03 (Captain: 「照你建議」, answering 「決定：B 照原設計修，讓追加指示紀錄也算進同症狀的輪數嗎？」, Captain amendment 1 of `diagnosis-rounds-count-toward-step-back`, superseding no criterion): a supported `<stage>-N-message-M.md` follow-up is a dispatch round on its own symptom, as the approved design states. Both disk and committed-state readers count it; record number, then message number, gives numeric order, with the plain record before its messages. The third counted record dates clearing whether it is plain or a follow-up.
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Save and check a stage dispatch record before building its Spacedock envelope."""

import argparse
import hashlib
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import stat
import subprocess
import sys

from design_surfaces import task_folder
from number_guards import Misconfigured, frontmatter

SCRIPTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def git(root, *args):
    return subprocess.run(["git", "--literal-pathspecs", "-C", str(root), *args], check=True,
                          capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()


def resolve_scope(args):
    value = frontmatter(args.workflow_dir / "README.md").get("state", "")
    relative = Path(value)
    if relative.is_absolute() or ".." in relative.parts:
        raise ValueError(f"{str(args.workflow_dir / 'README.md')!r}: unsupported state path")
    container = args.workflow_dir if value in ("", "$inline") else args.workflow_dir / relative
    if container.resolve(strict=True) != container:
        raise ValueError(f"{str(container)!r}: symlinked state directory")
    state = Path(git(container, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")).resolve(strict=True)
    if not container.is_relative_to(state) or (value not in ("", "$inline") and state != container):
        raise ValueError(f"{str(container)!r}: unsupported state repository layout")
    entity = args.entity_path
    folder = task_folder(entity)
    if (args.entity_input != entity or entity.suffix != ".md"
            or (entity.parent.parent if entity.name == "index.md" else entity.parent) != container):
        raise ValueError(f"{str(args.entity_input)!r}: unsupported or symlinked task layout")
    for directory in (folder, folder / "dispatch"):
        if os.path.lexists(directory) and (directory.is_symlink() or not directory.is_dir()):
            raise ValueError(f"{str(directory)!r}: unsupported task directory type")
    scope = [folder] if entity.name == "index.md" else [entity, folder]
    return state, folder, [path.relative_to(state).as_posix() for path in scope]


def check_task_scope(state, scope):
    def read(*flags):
        try:
            return subprocess.run(["git", "--literal-pathspecs", "-C", str(state), *flags],
                                  check=True, capture_output=True,
                                  env={**os.environ, "GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS": "0"}).stdout
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as error:
            raise ValueError(f"{str(state / scope[0])!r}: cannot inspect task scope ({flags[0]})") from error

    def refuse(name, condition):
        raise ValueError(f"{str(state / os.fsdecode(name))!r}: {condition}")

    head = {}
    for entry in read("ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "HEAD", "--", *scope).split(b"\0"):
        if entry:
            metadata, name = entry.split(b"\t", 1)
            mode, kind, oid = metadata.split()
            if kind != b"blob" or mode not in (b"100644", b"100755"):
                refuse(name, "unsupported HEAD type")
            head[name] = (mode, oid)
    index = {}
    for entry in read("ls-files", "--stage", "-z", "--", *scope).split(b"\0"):
        if entry:
            metadata, name = entry.split(b"\t", 1)
            mode, oid, stage = metadata.split()
            if stage != b"0":
                refuse(name, "unresolved index conflict")
            index[name] = (mode, oid)
    for entry in read("ls-files", "-v", "-z", "--", *scope).split(b"\0"):
        if entry and (entry[:1].islower() or entry[:1] == b"S"):
            refuse(entry[2:], "unsupported assume-unchanged or skip-worktree index flag")
    for name in sorted(head.keys() | index.keys()):
        if head.get(name) != index.get(name):
            refuse(name, "staged content, existence or mode differs from HEAD")
    algorithm = read("rev-parse", "--show-object-format").strip().decode("ascii")
    for name, (mode, oid) in index.items():
        path = state / os.fsdecode(name)
        try:
            info = path.lstat()
            if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) or path.resolve(strict=True) != path:
                refuse(name, "unsupported worktree type or path escape")
            data = path.read_bytes()
        except OSError as error:
            refuse(name, f"unstaged missing or unreadable worktree file ({error.strerror})")
        actual_mode = b"100755" if info.st_mode & stat.S_IXUSR else b"100644"
        actual_oid = hashlib.new(algorithm, b"blob " + str(len(data)).encode() + b"\0" + data).hexdigest().encode()
        if (actual_mode, actual_oid) != (mode, oid):
            refuse(name, "unstaged content or mode differs from index")
    for name in read("ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "-z", "--", *scope).split(b"\0"):
        if name:
            refuse(name, "untracked non-ignored task file")


def record_text(args, number, dispatched, checklist, notes):
    annotation = "workflow checkout" + (f", {args.note}" if args.note else "")
    header = [f"# {args.stage}-{number}", f"Dispatched: {dispatched} ({annotation})", f"Model: {args.model}"]
    if args.roster:
        header.append(f"Roster: {args.roster}")
    header += [f"Candidate: {sha}" for sha in args.candidate]
    if args.symptom:
        header.append(f"Symptom: {args.symptom}")
    return "\n".join(header) + "\n\n## Checklist\n" + checklist + "\n## Scope notes\n" + notes


def select_record(args, folder, dispatched, checklist, notes):
    state = Path(git(args.entity_path.parent, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"))
    directory = folder / "dispatch"
    relative = directory.relative_to(state).as_posix()
    pattern = re.compile(rf"{re.escape(args.stage)}-([1-9][0-9]*)\.md")
    committed = git(state, "ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "--name-only", "HEAD", "--", relative).split("\0")
    numbers = [int(match[1]) for path in committed
               if (match := pattern.fullmatch(Path(path).name)) and Path(path).parent.as_posix() == relative]
    newest = max(numbers, default=0)
    if newest:
        path = directory / f"{args.stage}-{newest}.md"
        rel = path.relative_to(state).as_posix()
        expected = record_text(args, newest, dispatched, checklist, notes)
        added = git(state, "log", "-1", "--diff-filter=A", "--format=%H", "--", rel)
        if (added == git(state, "rev-parse", "HEAD") and path.is_file()
                and path.read_bytes() == expected.encode("utf-8")):
            return path, False
    path = directory / f"{args.stage}-{newest + 1}.md"
    if git(state, "ls-files", "--", path.relative_to(state).as_posix()):
        raise FileExistsError(f"record already exists in index: {path}")
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("xb") as output:
        output.write(record_text(args, newest + 1, dispatched, checklist, notes).encode("utf-8"))
    return path, True


def remove_uncommitted(path, wrote):
    if wrote:
        state = Path(git(path.parent, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"))
        relative = path.relative_to(state).as_posix()
        committed = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(state), "cat-file", "-e", f"HEAD:{relative}"], capture_output=True)
        if committed.returncode:
            subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(state), "update-index", "--force-remove", "--", relative], check=True)
            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def parse_args(argv):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    for name in ("workflow-dir", "entity-path", "checklist-file", "scope-notes-file"):
        parser.add_argument(f"--{name}", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--stage", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    for name in ("roster", "symptom", "note"):
        parser.add_argument(f"--{name}")
    parser.add_argument("--candidate", action="append", default=[])
    parser.add_argument("--spacedock", default=os.environ.get("SPACEDOCK_BIN") or "spacedock")
    parser.add_argument("--host", choices=("claude", "codex", "pi"))
    parser.add_argument("--feedback-context-file", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--feedback-reflow", action="store_true")
    mode = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    mode.add_argument("--advance", action="store_true")
    mode.add_argument("--bare-mode", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", args.stage):
        parser.error("--stage must be a stage name")
    if any(not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{40}", sha) for sha in args.candidate):
        parser.error("--candidate must be a full 40-hex SHA")
    try:
        args.entity_input = Path(os.path.abspath(args.entity_path))
        for name in ("workflow_dir", "entity_path", "checklist_file", "scope_notes_file", "feedback_context_file"):
            value = getattr(args, name)
            if value is not None:
                setattr(args, name, value.resolve(strict=True))
        checklist = args.checklist_file.read_text()
        notes = args.scope_notes_file.read_text()
        dispatched = git(args.workflow_dir, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
    except (OSError, UnicodeError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
        parser.error(str(error))
    return args, dispatched, checklist, notes


def main(argv=None):
    args, dispatched, checklist, notes = parse_args(argv)
    try:
        state, folder, scope = resolve_scope(args)
        check_task_scope(state, scope)
        path, wrote = select_record(args, folder, dispatched, checklist, notes)
    except (OSError, ValueError, Misconfigured, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
        print(f"dispatch_stage: dispatch not built; {error}. "
              "Have the owner preserve and reconcile staged/worktree versions, then intentionally commit them; "
              "do not blindly state commit divergent data.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    checks = [subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-B", str(SCRIPTS / "dispatch_records.py"), *map(str, flags)],
                             capture_output=True, text=True)
              for flags in ((task_folder(args.entity_path),), ("--names", "--strict", path))]
    if any(check.returncode for check in checks):
        remove_uncommitted(path, wrote)
        print("dispatch_stage: dispatch not built; repair the dispatch record:", file=sys.stderr)
        for check in checks:
            if check.returncode:
                sys.stderr.write(check.stdout + check.stderr)
        return 1
    for line in dict.fromkeys(line for check in checks for line in check.stderr.splitlines(keepends=True)):
        sys.stderr.write(line)
    # see docs/adr/0070-stage-worker-dispatches-are-built-by-a-package-script-that-writes-their-record.md
    command = [args.spacedock, "dispatch", "build", "--advance" if args.advance else "--stamp"]
    for name in ("workflow_dir", "entity_path", "stage", "checklist_file", "scope_notes_file", "host", "feedback_context_file"):
        value = getattr(args, name)
        if value is not None:
            command += ["--" + name.replace("_", "-"), str(value)]
    command += ["--" + name.replace("_", "-") for name in ("feedback_reflow", "bare_mode") if getattr(args, name)]
    try:
        build = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True)
    except OSError as error:
        remove_uncommitted(path, wrote)
        print(f"dispatch_stage: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    sys.stderr.write(build.stderr)
    if build.returncode:
        remove_uncommitted(path, wrote)
        return build.returncode
    if args.advance:
        slug = args.entity_path.parent.name if args.entity_path.name == "index.md" else args.entity_path.stem
        commit = subprocess.run([args.spacedock, "state", "commit", slug, "--workflow-dir", str(args.workflow_dir)],
                                capture_output=True, text=True)
        sys.stderr.write(commit.stderr)
        if commit.returncode:
            sys.stderr.write(commit.stdout)
            return 1
    sys.stdout.write(build.stdout)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Mutate isolated package copies and require the preservation oracle to fail."""
import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument('--code-root', type=Path, required=True)
parser.add_argument('--output-dir', type=Path, required=True)
a = parser.parse_args()
a.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
source = a.code_root / 'kc-dev-flow-2'
original = (source / 'scripts/dispatch_stage.py').read_text()
guard = '        check_task_scope(state, scope)\n'
selected = '[(folder / "dispatch" / f"{args.stage}-1.md").relative_to(state).as_posix()]'
mutants = [
 ('guard-removed', guard, '', None, 'test_retry_preserves_staged_record_with_worktree_at_head'),
 ('index-comparison-omitted', 'if head.get(name) != index.get(name):', 'if False:', 'flat:fresh:report:equal-change', None),
 ('worktree-comparison-omitted', 'if (actual_mode, actual_oid) != (mode, oid):', 'if False:', 'folder:fresh:report:worktree-only', None),
 ('untracked-check-omitted', 'for name in read("ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "-z", "--", *scope).split(b"\\0"):', 'for name in ():', 'flat:fresh:new-report:untracked', None),
 ('scope-only-selected-record', guard, '        check_task_scope(state, ' + selected + ')\n', 'flat:fresh:task:staged-only', None),
 ('scope-only-dispatch-directory', guard, '        check_task_scope(state, [(folder / "dispatch").relative_to(state).as_posix()])\n', 'folder:fresh:report:partial', None),
 ('guard-after-record-creation', guard + '        path, wrote = select_record(args, folder, dispatched, checklist, notes)\n', '        path, wrote = select_record(args, folder, dispatched, checklist, notes)\n' + guard, 'flat:fresh:report:staged-only', None),
 ('retry-bypasses-guard', guard, '        if not any((folder / "dispatch").glob(f"{args.stage}-*.md")):\n    ' + guard, 'flat:retry:reused:staged-only', None),
 ('advance-bypasses-guard', guard, '        if not args.advance:\n    ' + guard, 'folder:advance:reused:staged-only', None),
]
results = []
for name, old, new, case, method in mutants:
    assert original.count(old) == 1, (name, original.count(old))
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='dispatch-scope-mutant-') as tmp:
        root = Path(tmp) / 'kc-dev-flow-2'
        shutil.copytree(source, root, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns('__pycache__', '*.pyc'))
        (root / 'scripts/dispatch_stage.py').write_text(original.replace(old, new))
        log_path = a.output_dir / (name + '.snapshots.jsonl')
        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE='1', DISPATCH_SCOPE_LOG=str(log_path))
        env.pop('DISPATCH_SCOPE_CASE', None)
        if case:
            env['DISPATCH_SCOPE_CASE'] = case
        command = [sys.executable, '-B', str(root / 'scripts/test_dispatch_stage.py'),
                   'DispatchStageTests.' + (method or 'test_scope_preservation_matrix')]
        result = subprocess.run(command, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=90)
        output = result.stdout + result.stderr
        (a.output_dir / (name + '.log')).write_text(output)
        snapshots = [json.loads(line) for line in log_path.read_text().splitlines()] if log_path.exists() else []
        caught = bool(result.returncode and 'FAIL:' in output and 'refusal changed scoped or outside state' in output
                      and snapshots and any(row['before'] != row['after'] for row in snapshots))
        results.append(dict(name=name, status='passed' if caught else 'failed', mutant_exit=result.returncode,
                            scenario=case or 'reported-retry', oracle='snapshot preservation',
                            message='Mutant must fail its matching preservation assertion'))
        (a.output_dir / 'results.json').write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2) + '\n')
        print(json.dumps(results[-1]), flush=True)
sys.exit(any(row['status'] != 'passed' for row in results))

"""Refuse candidates that change an applied migration or take a number another task holds, and reserve numbers per task.

check   exit 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 misconfiguration. Rules: R1 a migration present at the merge-base is
        modified or deleted; R2 the same against every 'Applied at: <env> <sha>' commit; R3 an added migration
        number is not above the base tip's highest; R4 an added migration or ADR number is not in the task's
        'Migration:' / 'ADR:' lines; R5 an added ADR number exists on the base tip; R6 a task whose frontmatter says
        'profile: poc' differs from the merge-base anywhere under the migrations directory; R7 (only under
        'migrations-path: none') the candidate adds a file named NNNN_name.sql anywhere; R8 an added ADR
        number absent from the base tip is held by another live task.
        'migrations-path: none' declares that the repository has no migration files: R1 to R3 and R6 are skipped,
        the ADR rules R4, R5 and R8 still run, and a db task is no longer exit 2.
reserve prints 'Migration: NNNN' or 'ADR: NNNN' (one above the base tip and every other live task, never
        filling a gap); a task that already holds a line gets it back. One number per kind per task.
Holders: own state *.md and */index.md, plus every origin/spacedock-state/* branch fetched explicitly.
        The checked task's path is excluded on its own branch only when its state checkout has origin.
Limits: only files named NNNN_name.sql count as migrations, so meta/_journal.json and snapshots are not checked (R6 does check them);
a deploy nobody recorded as 'Applied at:' is not detected; run 'git -C <repo> fetch' first, the base tip is what is local.
Task lines are read from the task's '## Number guards' section.
"""
import argparse
import posixpath
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

MIGRATION = re.compile(r"^(\d+)_.+\.sql$")
ADR = re.compile(r"^(\d{4})-.+\.md$")
NO_MIGRATIONS = "none"
KINDS = {"migration": ("Migration", MIGRATION), "adr": ("ADR", ADR)}


class Misconfigured(Exception):
    pass


def git(repo, *args):
    done = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if done.returncode:
        raise Misconfigured(f"git {' '.join(args)}: {done.stderr.strip()}")
    return done.stdout


def resolve(repo, ref, what="ref"):
    done = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{ref}^{{commit}}"],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)
    if done.returncode:
        raise Misconfigured(f"cannot resolve {what} '{ref}' in {repo}")
    return done.stdout.strip()


def frontmatter(readme):
    if not readme.is_file():
        raise Misconfigured(f"no workflow README at {readme}")
    return frontmatter_text(readme.read_text())


def frontmatter_text(text):
    lines = text.split("\n")
    found = {}
    for line in lines[1:] if lines[0] == "---" else []:
        if line == "---":
            break
        match = re.match(r"^([\w-]+):[ \t]*(.*?)[ \t]*$", line)
        if match:
            found[match.group(1)] = match.group(2).strip("'\"")
    return found


def task_facts(path):
    task = Path(path)
    if not task.is_file():
        raise Misconfigured(f"task file {task} does not exist")
    return task_facts_text(task.read_text(errors="replace"))


def task_facts_text(text):
    section = re.search(r"^## Number guards[ \t]*\n(.*?)(?=^## |\Z)", text, re.M | re.S)
    body = section.group(1) if section else ""
    surfaces = re.search(r"^Surfaces:(.*)$", text, re.M)
    return {
        "migration": {int(n) for n in re.findall(r"^Migration:[ \t]*(\d+)[ \t]*$", body, re.M)},
        "adr": {int(n) for n in re.findall(r"^ADR:[ \t]*(\d+)[ \t]*$", body, re.M)},
        "applied": re.findall(r"^Applied at:[ \t]*(\S+)[ \t]+([0-9a-f]{7,40})[ \t]*$", body, re.M),
        "poc": frontmatter_text(text).get("profile") == "poc",
        "surfaces": set(re.split(r"[\s,]+", surfaces.group(1).strip())) if surfaces else set(),
    }

## Never write git config from a worktree of this repository

### Applicability

When a worker, validator or acceptance script for this repository would exercise a
failure path by writing git configuration (for example `git remote set-url origin
...`, `git config`) from inside a worktree checkout, including the Captain's main
checkout or any worktree of the repository.

### Practice

Do not write git config in any worktree of this repository: every worktree shares
one config, so one write changes every checkout. Run such a step only in a throwaway
`git clone` in a temp directory, and say so in the dispatch scope notes and in the
acceptance script. If a shared value is changed by mistake, restore it from a
recorded original, so record the original value before any config read-modify step.
Bounded: one observed incident; this does not show the ban alone prevented a repeat,
since the acceptance script was also moved into a throwaway clone.

### Evidence

Validation cycle 1 of workflow-checkout-must-match-trunk-readme
(iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins#631) ran `git remote set-url` in a worktree and rewrote
remote.origin.url for every worktree to /nonexistent/origin.git. The validator
restored it by inference (sibling clone and PR repository; the original value was
not recorded) and FO confirmed it against FETCH_HEAD from before the incident. The
later cycles carried an explicit ban in the dispatch records (implementation-2,
implementation-4, validation-2, validation-3) and ran that step in a throwaway clone
with remote.origin.url identical before and after; no repeat was observed in those
cycles. Recorded in
spacedock-state/dev2:_archive/workflow-checkout-must-match-trunk-readme.md at
closure revision 173fd173224bac844133b87d6ca1ef99d9eb25b7 (validation Summary of
cycle 1 and the dispatch/ records). Existing rules checked: implementation
principles ban only `git stash` for the same shared-state reason; the workflow
README's Review-finding disposition allows throwaway-checkout probes but never says
a worktree config write is forbidden, so no rule states this practice.

## Measure the words FO reads at each moment, not one file's size

### Applicability

A kc-dev-flow-2 change whose goal is to cut what First Officer (FO) reads, such as
moving rule text out of the adopted README (references/sd/workflow.md) into a mod,
a script's printed output or another file, where acceptance is stated as a word
count.

### Practice

State the acceptance number as the words FO reads at each lifecycle moment
(startup, idle on an open PR, idle on a merged PR, after the archive, the merge
ask): every passage and every script output that instructs a step due at that
moment, counted the same way for the unchanged base and for the candidate, with
each moment required to fall below its base. Do not accept the size of the one
file the text left (for example WORKFLOW_WORD_BUDGET in
kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/lint-skills.py) as the measure, because that number can fall
while FO's total reading rises. Bounded: one task; the redesign also gave each
step one home, so the count is not shown to be the only cause of the reduction;
the recount script lives only in the archived task's validation folder, not in the
repository; and a validator found the first recount script under-counted one
moment, so recount with an independent copy.

### Evidence

In task fo-lifecycle-mod (iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins#643, closure revision
d2c1d80085b2699e4cad79eecd4c13fe2230647d) the first design's criterion AC-2
bounded only references/sd/workflow.md words (5561 down to 5483); validation
recommended PASSED at that design, yet FO then measured FO's total reading as up
by about 507 words while the README shrank by 80, and the Captain sent the task
back (amendment 3). The redo counted words FO reads per moment, and the landed mod
cut that total from 2036 to 1699 with every moment lower. Recorded in
spacedock-state/dev2:_archive/fo-lifecycle-mod.md under '### Why the cycle-2
design grew' and '### Words FO reads at each moment', and in the Cycle 1 FO line

states this practice.

## List every input before promising a verdict survives later history

### Applicability

A kc-dev-flow-2 task in this repository that designs or reviews a check run over
committed history (such as the state-branch laws runner) and promises that a
violation, once committed, keeps its verdict after later commits (for example "stays
red until an anchor moves"), or that answers a review finding of the form "a later
change erases a committed violation".

### Practice

Before the design gate, list every input the verdict reads (files read at the run
revision, task files enumerated at the tip, the README or config passed in at run
time) and write the persistence promise as one property test: after the event,
commit every later change the history allows (edit, delete, archive, rename, and a
change to each run-time input) and require the same exit code and output. When a
review finding of this class arrives, treat it as a finding about that list: add the
input it names and every sibling input to the list and to the test in the same
cycle, instead of repairing the one reported read. If an input cannot be pinned to
the event, narrow or drop the promise in the design and ask the Captain, rather than
shipping an absolute that later history can undo. Uncertain: whether this ordering
would have avoided the rework, since the Captain's actual ruling was to drop the
